title: Complaint, grievance, inquest, lawsuit, review, and investigation as delayed grief language

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source and seed-brief synthesis for rev0023 institutional-opacity layer; no private testimony, no public rendering, no facility-specific allegation, no legal/clinical/facility advice.
source_packet.collection_method: manual public-source extraction, source-card routing, and seed-cue factoring during rev0023
limitations: Sources support vocabulary, official-trace boundaries, institutional review gates, and source-bias awareness only.
No individual case facts, facility names, private family narrative, staff accusation, medical allegation, legal conclusion, or procedure instruction is admitted from this record.
Public rendering, if ever attempted, requires institution-specific, legal/jurisdictional, ethics, privacy, equity, and publication-language review.

moment.plain_scene: After an institutional death, grief may be accompanied by complaint, grievance, inquest, lawsuit, external review, internal review, public-record request, or unanswered correspondence; the archive can name the language without guiding the process.
ordinary_language_queries: file complaint after institutional death words

content_layers.observation_text: After an institutional death, grief may be accompanied by complaint, grievance, inquest, lawsuit, external review, internal review, public-record request, or unanswered correspondence; the archive can name the language without guiding the process.
content_layers.source_synthesis: The sources support treating this as a closed-room / institutional-opacity record: official categories, reporting systems, review terms, access rules, and public data can orient the cube, but they do not by themselves tell the whole human story of the death.
content_layers.witness_language: Families, staff, advocates, investigators, and official systems may use different words for the same death. This record preserves the distinction without deciding a case.
content_layers.reader_boundary: A reader may arrive with fear, anger, suspicion, shame, or confusion. The archive can name the relevant language and the limits of the evidence; it cannot tell them what happened in a specific institution.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Future work must route this record through institutional-opacity, official-trace, legal/jurisdictional, privacy, equity, clinical if applicable, cultural if applicable, and publication-language review before any public rendering.
language_notes: Say closed room, restricted access, official trace, reporting category, review, notification, family access, or institutional account when those words are source-supported.
Do not imply culpability, innocence, neglect, abuse, preventability, or official completeness without case-specific authority and review.
Do not turn accountability language into public accusation or procedural advice.
content_layers.what_this_is_not: Not legal advice, not medical advice, not facility advice, not crisis response, not an investigation manual, not a facility-ranking tool, not public accusation, and not evidence that any named institution caused or prevented a death.

provenance.provenance_statement: Added in rev0023 from public-source synthesis and seed-cue factoring; no private account, no case-specific official validation, no legal/clinical validation, no public release.

evidence_class.limitations: No private testimony, no case allegation, no facility identification, no legal/clinical/facility advice, no public release.

safety.identifiability_boundary: Do not include names, exact dates, facility names, staff names, badge numbers, room/unit identifiers, rare circumstances, videos, logs, screenshots, medical details, incident-report excerpts, or family facts that could identify a person or living survivor.
safety.medical_advice_risk: Do not use this record for diagnosis, treatment, prognosis, crisis care, withdrawal management, restraint/seclusion decisions, infection-control decisions, or clinical quality review.
safety.legal_or_facility_advice_risk: Do not infer legal rights, complaint routes, reporting duties, liability, negligence, neglect, abuse, malpractice, custodial responsibility, or facility policy from this record.
safety.cultural_or_ritual_risk: Do not universalize what families, traditions, staff, investigators, advocates, or institutions should say or do after an institutional death.
safety.clinical_boundary: This is not clinical, legal, facility, investigative, disciplinary, correctional, immigration, nursing-home, psychiatric, child-welfare, patient-safety, funeral, media, or advocacy advice; qualified local authorities and supports govern actual cases.
safety_notes: Institutional records are high risk for identification, retaliation, defamation, survivor harm, official overclaim, and public speculation.
An official record can be necessary and still incomplete; a family memory can be true and still not a legal finding.
The archive must never make silence, delay, data suppression, or missing access stand alone as proof of what happened.
